question: For experimental Claw updates, should the CLI's single exact `planIntegrity` confirmation be the approved consent mechanism for separately disclosed capability escalations, or must the CLI require an additional distinct acknowledgment before a later apply command can execute them?
rationale: The branch creates the core capability and consent contract used by the successor executor PR; source inspection of a planner cannot safely choose the permanent operator-security UX without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve integrity-bound consent
options.body: Treat a plan-integrity token as sufficient once the human and JSON previews separately disclose each capability escalation.

options.title: Require a separate escalation acknowledgment
options.body: Retain plan integrity for content and require a distinct CLI confirmation or flag whenever the plan contains capability escalations.

options.title: Keep planning internal for now
options.body: Pause this public CLI contract until the Claw lifecycle stack has a maintainer-approved end-to-end consent design.

recommendation.title: Approve integrity-bound consent
recommendation.body: Treat a plan-integrity token as sufficient once the human and JSON previews separately disclose each capability escalation.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick is assigned to this PR and authored the review requirements governing the planner’s authoritative pre-consent behavior.
